nodes.name: Ni/Ni(OH)₂ core-shell electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The Ni/Ni(OH)₂ catalyst consisting of Ni nanosphere core and Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet shell was synthesized via one-step electrodeposition in aqueous NiCl₂ solution on carbon paper. The alteration of NiCl₂ concentration during electrolysis induced a subtle variation in pH value, which in turn triggered the formation of the core-shell structure (shell thickness 10-30 nm, nanospheres <400 nm diameter).

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: one-step electrodeposition in aqueous NiCl₂ solution

nodes.source_text: The Ni/Ni(OH)₂ catalyst consisting of Ni core and Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet shell was synthesized via one-step electrodeposition in aqueous NiCl₂ solution, as illustrated in Figure 1a. The alteration of NiCl₂ concentration during electrolysis induced a subtle variation in pH value, which in turn triggered the formation of the core-shell structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/Ni(OH)₂ and Ni nanoparticles show sharp diffraction peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76.4° corresponding to (111), (200), and (220) planes of face-centered cubic Ni (JCPDS No. 04-0850). Ni(OH)₂ shows subtle peaks indicating poor crystallinity (JCPDS No. 38-0715).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XRD pattern of the as-prepared Ni/Ni(OH)₂ heterostructure and Ni nanoparticles, the sharp and obvious diffraction peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76.4° correspond to the (111), (200) and (220) crystal planes of Ni ... crystallinity of Ni(OH)₂ in Ni/Ni(OH)₂ and Ni(OH)₂ catalysts is very poor.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/Ni(OH)₂ consists of nanospheres <400 nm diameter with ultra-thin nanosheets growing on the surface giving furry appearance. Ni shows flower-like nanoparticles and Ni(OH)₂ shows nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) reveals that the Ni/Ni(OH)₂ sample consists of numerous nanospheres with a diameter of less than 400 nm, and the furry appearance is caused by the ultra-thin nanosheets ... morphology of flower-like Ni nanoparticles and Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets can be observed.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Subsequently, the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) reveals that Ni/Ni(OH)₂ is mainly composed of crystalline Ni and almost amorphous Ni(OH)₂ ... consistent with XRD analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM with EDS shows homogeneous Ni and O distribution in Ni/Ni(OH)₂ nanosphere.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As indicated in the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and the corresponding energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mappings, the distribution of Ni and O is homogeneous.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS line scan shows higher Ni than O content in core and similar Ni:O content in Ni/Ni(OH)₂ shell (10-30 nm thick).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The linear EDS scan reveals a higher content of Ni than that of O in the core area and a similar content of Ni and O in the shell area ... core-shell Ni/Ni(OH)₂ possesses a shell thickness between 10 and 30 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms Ni/Ni(OH)₂, Ni, and Ni(OH)₂ contain Ni and O elements. Ni 2p shows Ni⁰ (852.6/869.9 eV) in Ni/Ni(OH)₂ and Ni, Ni²⁺ (855.5/861.6, 873.2/879.5 eV) in all. Lower Ni⁰:Ni²⁺ intensity ratio in Ni/Ni(OH)₂ indicates Ni(OH)₂ surface dominance. Quantitative: Ni/Ni(OH)₂ 69.15% Ni, Ni 77.43% Ni, Ni(OH)₂ 32.60% Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) survey spectra of Ni/Ni(OH)₂, Ni, and Ni(OH)₂ ... indicate their elemental composition is Ni and O. In the XPS fine spectra, the Ni 2p spectra ... characteristic peaks of Ni⁰ with binding energies at 852.6 eV and 869.9 eV manifest the existence of metallic Ni in the Ni/Ni(OH)₂ and Ni samples. Ulteriorly, we assessed the peak intensities ... lower intensity of Ni⁰ in Ni/Ni(OH)₂ compared to Ni²⁺, indicating that Ni(OH)₂ is the primary constituent of its surface ... quantitatively analyses of the Ni 2p and O 1s spectra show that the atomic content of Ni in Ni/Ni(OH)₂ is 69.15% which is lower than the 77.43% in the Ni sample, but significantly higher than the 32.60% found in the Ni(OH)₂ sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS depth profiling of Ni/Ni(OH)₂ shows Ni⁰ peak intensity increases and Ni²⁺ decreases with etching depth. Surface: Ni 69.15%, O 30.85%; bulk stabilizes at Ni ~90%, O ~10%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS depth profiling ... peak intensity of Ni⁰ increases with depth while that of Ni²⁺ decreases ... atomic percentages of Ni and O are 69.15% and 30.85% on the Ni/Ni(OH)₂ surface and gradually stabilize to ~90% and ~10%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Ni and Ni(OH)₂ in Ni/Ni(OH)₂ are interconvertible according to applied potential: Ni(OH)₂ band at 478 cm⁻¹ decreases under reduction (Ni(OH)₂→Ni), increases at more negative potentials (Ni→Ni(OH)₂ by NO₃⁻).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy reveals Ni and Ni(OH)₂ are interconvertible according to the applied potential ... The initial broad band at 478 cm⁻¹, associated with Ni(OH)₂, persists ... intensity of the characteristic peak decreases apparently, once a reduction potential is exerted ... When the applied potential is decreased to -0.276 V ... intensity of the characteristic peak increases again.
